headline: Crude pulls back from the Hormuz run as grains sit quiet
lead: Corn is at $5.01 overnight, basically flat, holding the line it has worked to defend since getting back over $5 on Monday. Crude eased 1.0% to $90.60 after a 4.9% run Wednesday, with Brent still above $100 on Hormuz tanker disruptions, ongoing since July and flaring again this week.
teaser: Corn holds flat at $5.01 while crude gives back some of its Hormuz-driven jump.

one_number.unit: Corn Belt states short on storage
one_number.context: Farmdoc says the Belt can hold this year's carry-in and harvest overall, but ten of thirteen states fall short locally.

sections.title: Corn holds the round number again
sections.body:
- Corn is at **$5.01** overnight, up half a cent, the fourth straight session parked right at $5.
- Farmdoc's new storage study says the Corn Belt can hold this year's crop in aggregate, but ten of thirteen states are short on local space.
sections.so_what: A flat board can still hide real local basis pressure at harvest.

sections.title: Beans firm, meal leads the complex
sections.body:
- Soybeans are at **$12.94** overnight, up five cents, with meal up 1.5% to $366.00 after Wednesday's bigger 3.5% jump.
- Soybean oil added 0.3% to $67.62, a small bounce after Wednesday's 3.1% drop tied to the crude and biofuel policy shift.
sections.so_what: Meal is still doing more work than beans or oil in this rally.

sections.title: Crude gives a little back
sections.body:
- WTI is at **$90.60** overnight, down 1.0%, pulling back after Wednesday's 4.9% jump on a fresh tanker hit near Qatar.
- Brent is still above $100, with tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz at a two-month low on the ongoing Iran-Hormuz cycle, a pattern that has built and unwound twice since spring.
sections.so_what: Diesel relief from China matters more to fall fieldwork costs than the crude headline.

outside_the_pit.title: ARC and PLC payments set a record for 2025 crop year
outside_the_pit.body: USDA says farm safety net programs will pay out $13.8 billion for 2025, the largest gross payout in the programs' history.

watch_list.desc: Corn back under $5.00 would say harvest supply is winning again after four days at the line.
Another Hormuz tanker incident could push WTI back toward $95; a calm weekend could ease it toward $88.
Crop Progress report, the next read on harvest pace against storage capacity limits.

source_summary: CME/CBOT locked price table, farmdocdaily.illinois.edu, oilprice.com, feedstuffs.com, world-grain.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $5.01 vs $4.62 projected (+8.4%), 6 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.89 vs $11.09 projected (+16.2%), 5 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: USDA RMA, as of Oct 8. Oct 1-31 window, most states.
